elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 expressly states that Vendor shall defend Customer.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 expressly states that Vendor shall indemnify Customer from claims and resulting damages, costs, and expenses.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity obligations must extend to Customer's Affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 expressly names Customer and its Affiliates as beneficiaries.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity must cover claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(a) covers allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(b) covers Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity must cover claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires the indemnified Party to give prompt written notice.

elements.element: The indemnifying party must control the defence of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 provides that the indemnifying Party shall control the defence.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation in the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 requires the indemnified Party to provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers claims arising out of Customer-provided content.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 covers claims arising out of Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must contain no trigger other than Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 20.1 limits the operative triggers to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims involving the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2(a) provides Vendor indemnity for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the rendered clause, and the absence of potentially relevant modifications is not demonstrated.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with non-Vendor products, services, or materials.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause, and the absence of potentially relevant combinations is not demonstrated.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the rendered clause, and the absence of potentially relevant specifications is not demonstrated.

elements.element: For covered IP claims, Vendor must have an obligation to procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation to procure continued use rights.

elements.element: For covered IP claims, Vendor must have an obligation to modify the affected item so it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP claims, Vendor must have an obligation to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP claims, Vendor must provide a refund remedy if the other specified remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No operative liability cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap is included; only the Section 21 heading is shown.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position by narrowing Customer's indemnity, adding the required Vendor indemnity triggers and beneficiaries, and supplying notice, control, and cooperation procedures. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its exclusions, IP remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The changes are substantively targeted and preserve unrelated terms, although Sections 20.2 and 20.3 are awkwardly placed after the Section 21 heading and should be moved before that heading.
